claims.claim: Ants are eusocial insects whose colonies can range from a few dozen individuals to millions.
claims.evidence: Direct statement in Ant source about eusociality and colony size range.
claims.quote: Ants are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae

claims.claim: Nearly all ant colonies include one or more fertile females called queens, along with fertile males called drones.
claims.evidence: Source explicitly mentions fertile queens and drones in nearly all colonies.
claims.quote: Nearly all ant colonies also have some fertile males called "drones" and one or more fertile females called "queens" (gynes).

claims.claim: Most colony members are sterile, wingless female workers called ergates.
claims.evidence: Source states that most sterile wingless females are workers (ergates).

claims.claim: Typical colonies consist of various castes of sterile, wingless females, most of which are workers, as well as soldiers and other specialised groups.
claims.evidence: Source directly describes typical colony composition.
claims.quote: Typical colonies consist of various castes of sterile, wingless females, most of which are workers (ergates), as well as soldiers (dinergates) and other specialised groups.

claims.claim: Some colonies occupy large territories with sizeable nests, and supercolonies can reach hundreds of millions of individuals.
claims.evidence: Source mentions large territories and supercolony size.
claims.quote: Some colonies occupy large territories with sizeable nest (or nests) that consist of millions of individuals. In some cases they reach hundreds of millions of individuals in super colonies.

claims.claim: In some lineages, such as army ants, the colony does not construct a permanent nest and moves almost incessantly.
claims.evidence: Army ant source states colonies lack permanent nests and move incessantly.
claims.quote: army ants do not construct permanent nests; an army ant colony moves almost incessantly

claims.claim: Ant colonies are described as superorganisms because the ants appear to operate as a unified entity.
claims.evidence: Source directly links superorganism description to unified entity operation.
claims.quote: The colonies are described as superorganisms because the ants appear to operate as a unified entity

claims.claim: Ants have colonised almost every landmass on Earth; the only places lacking indigenous ants are Antarctica and a few remote or inhospitable islands.
claims.evidence: Source states colonization extent and the only ant‑free places.
claims.quote: Ants have colonised almost every landmass on Earth. The only places lacking indigenous ants are Antarctica and a few remote or inhospitable islands.
